name: Collide Capital
identity_check: Confirmed as Collide Capital (collidecap.com; LinkedIn company page linked from the site, HQ New York, NY), the early-stage VC firm co-founded by Aaron Samuels (ex-Blavity/AfroTech) and Brian Hollins (ex-Goldman Sachs growth equity) that invests pre-seed to Series A in fintech, supply chain and future of work. Its own press page links the April 2026 TechCrunch, ImpactAlpha and AfroTech coverage of its $95M Fund II. Not Collider Ventures (Israel), and not 'Collide', the Houston GenAI energy startup that shows up in database searches.

requires_us_entity: unknown. Nothing stated; the portfolio includes companies the site places in Colombia (Creditop), Mexico (OneCarNow!, Jelou) and Israel (Weav), but their legal domiciles were not checked.

Two pitch forms: the header button and FAQ ('Pitch us here') point to the Airtable form recorded as application_url; the portfolio and 'Ready to Collide?' sections point to a Typeform (2xrdf64xib2.typeform.com/PitchCollide). The FAQ says the investment team reviews every inbound pitch. A separate LP-contact email exists (not recorded).

SEC EDGAR: the full-text search API accepted the 'CapitalAtlas research' User-Agent, but www.sec.gov refused the Form D documents themselves, so offering amounts, sale dates and exact legal details of Fund I, Fund II, the NYS and MD SSBCI funds and the Revi and Slang SPVs were not read. Fund II's first Form D was filed 2024-09-27 (amended 2025-06-04), well before the April 2026 close announcement.

Fund close dates: Fund I only '2022' (TechCrunch; Fund I Form D filed 2022-02-10); Fund II date is the 2026-04-09 announcement, no final-close date published. Size of the 2019 'initial exploratory fund' (Pulse 2.0) is not disclosed.
SSBCI: TEDCO (Maryland, Jul 2025) selected Collide to manage and invest up to $10M of SSBCI money, matching the 'MD SSBCI Fund, LP' filing; the New York SSBCI allocation size was not found.

Partner focus sectors are not assigned by the firm and team bios do not give sector coverage, so focus_sectors are empty. Team page also lists Lauren Dupont (SVP of Operations), Shane Bates (Finance), Sabine Quetant (Marketing), Jovana Ruzic (Executive Assistant) and two 'Breakthrough Accelerator' members; not recorded as partners. Artificial Lawyer calls Aaron Samuels 'General Partner'; the team page says 'Founder and Managing Partner'.

Every card on collidecap.com/portfolio carries an 'ACQUIRED' label, including active companies such as Braven and Jelou; treated as a site template artifact, not as exit data. The firm reports five exits (AfroTech, Pulse 2.0) without naming them all (Butter Technologies is shown as acquired by GrubMarket on the homepage).

Rounds not recorded because no fetched round page named Collide: Cortex (AI-native electronics engineering, entered 2026; only a database hint of a ~$10M July 2026 seed), Ocho (Collide named as investor by ImpactAlpha but no round page), FaceSign, Art Lab, Anadyr, Heva, Gemist (VentureBeat piece names no investors), Tandem, TeamOhana, OCN Series B (Bloomberg link on Collide's press page, paywalled), Vendorflow (2021 round coverage does not name Collide).

Blocked round pages (403): Ellis on Business Wire, Helios AI on Produce Market Guide, Intramotev on Railway Age, Collide's own Fund II release on Business Wire (2026-04-09). Ellis's own release, as rendered, also listed Kearny Jackson among investors; not in Pulse 2.0's list, so left out of participants.

Company founding years not stated on round pages for Ellis, Braven, Prefix, Helios AI, Creditop, Flourish Care, Theo Ai, Intramotev and Coldcart; Ellis HQ (New York) comes from Collide's portfolio card.
